There are six unlabeled beakers, each representing a single solution from the list or a mix of equal volumes of two of the solutions. Beakers are noted as (1), (2), (3), (4), (5), (6). You are doing a series of tests to identify the components of these beakers. When mixing (1) and (2) a yellow-brown precipitate is formed. When mixing (1) and (3) a bright yellow precipitate is observed. Mixing (2) and (3) results in a dark red precipitate. Mixing (2) and (4) results in the same red precipitate, and gas bubbles are observed. When mixing (3) and (5) a white precipitate is formed. However, when an excess of (5) is added to (3) the precipitate dissolves. Mixing (3) and (6) results in a white precipitate. Mixing (4) and (5) also results in a white precipitate. When (6) is added to the mixture of (4) and (5) the precipitate dissolves and gas bubbles can be observed. When mixing (4) and (6) the solution gets cloudy and gas bubbles can be observed. When adding an excess of (6) to the solution of (4) and (6) the solution becomes clear. Mixing (5) and (6) results in a white precipitate. When adding an excess of (6) to the solution of (5) and (6) the precipitate dissolves. Which of the following are in one of the original six unlabeled beakers?

The white precipitate from (3)+(5) that dissolves in excess (5) suggests AgOH or Al(OH)₃, so (5) is likely NH₄OH.
The gas bubbles when (6) is added to mixtures suggests (6) is an acid or carbonate.
